  "run_id": "f72f7f513e9d",
  "round": 2,
  "topic": "empirical reply-to-proposition alignment in email and dialogue, focusing on partial replies, multiple questions, unanswered questions, and multi-proposition antecedents",
  "gaps": [
    {
      "id": "gap-1",
      "description": "Direct empirical evidence is still missing for proposition-level agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, and answer scope in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat, especially cases where one short response applies to only part of a preceding message.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"reply scope\" email dialogue proposition agreement approval rejection workplace communication"
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-2",
      "description": "A validated annotation and evaluation scheme is still missing for mapping workplace responses to exact proposition or span targets while representing exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, discontinuous, multiple-antecedent, and explicit no-link cases. Individual requirements are supported by the literature, but the combined msgloom annotation contract has not been validated.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "Resolve by defining the complete msgloom annotation contract, including target granularity, span/proposition representation, partial and discontinuous targets, multiple antecedents, ambiguity labels, unsupported/no-link cases, and adjudication rules; then validate it on a representative workplace email/chat sample using independent annotators. Measure inter-annotator agreement separately for link existence, target selection, relation type, ambiguity, and multi-antecedent structure, document disagreement categories, revise the guidelines, and establish an evaluation protocol and benchmark set."
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-3",
      "description": "Direct evidence remains insufficient for aligning replies to one or more questions when a preceding workplace message contains multiple questions, requests, or alternatives, including proposition-level detection of questions that remain unanswered.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"question answer alignment\" dialogue \"multiple questions\" partial answer unanswered questions"
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-4",
      "description": "It remains open whether and how a workplace response should be modeled as targeting a composite or multi-proposition antecedent. The corpus supports composite abstract discourse referents and multi-unit discourse antecedents, but does not directly evaluate multi-proposition reply scope in work communication.",
      "classification": "ACADEMIC",
      "priority": "MEDIUM",
      "status": "open",
      "suggested_search_query": "\"multi-antecedent\" propositional anaphora dialogue composite discourse referent reply"
    },
    {
      "id": "gap-5",
      "description": "The appropriate msgloom policy for uncertainty-driven abstention, ambiguity, missing antecedents, and asymmetric error costs remains unvalidated. The literature supports explicit no-link outcomes and preservation of ambiguous or multiple antecedents, but it does not establish confidence thresholds or the relative cost of over-broad approval/commitment links versus unresolved links.",
      "classification": "ENGINEERING",
      "priority": "HIGH",
      "status": "open",
      "resolution_notes": "Resolve by specifying an explicit product-risk cost model for false positive links, over-broad scope, incorrect approval or commitment attribution, false no-link decisions, and unresolved cases. Build a dedicated held-out benchmark containing ambiguous, missing-antecedent, no-link, partial-scope, and approval/commitment examples; calibrate model confidence on development data; compare abstention and decision thresholds using coverage-risk, precision/recall, calibration, and cost-weighted error metrics; and select thresholds and fallback behavior from the benchmark rather than inferring them from the literature."
    }
  ],
  "convergence": {
    "should_continue": true,
    "reason": "open_gaps_remain",
    "next_round_topic": "proposition-level response scope in workplace email and dialogue, with emphasis on partial replies to multi-question or multi-proposition antecedents, unanswered subquestions, approval/rejection scope, and multi-antecedent response links"
  }
}
